summary: Iteration 6 verifies (a) full removal of phone/WhatsApp from Ceramic & Yard flows (backend models, GETs, admin POST, CSV import, admin UI forms, dashboard rows) and (b) single-device login enforcement (JWT sid claim, active_session_id on user doc, forced-logout on the older token, /auth/logout $unset, register duplicate 400). All 8 backend pytest assertions PASS. Frontend: 11/11 UI checks for phone/WhatsApp removal PASS. Single-device forced-logout flow verified end-to-end: after a second admin login, navigating in context A triggers 401 which clears jp_token and redirects to /login; the backend server-side session is invalidated (subsequent /auth/me with old token returns 401). Header Logout button clears both server-side session and client-side jp_token and routes to /login. Two Playwright assertions failed as false-negatives due to timing (token check ran before login promise settled) and a Sonner toast selector mismatch — neither reflects an app bug.
critical_code_review_comments: AppHeader.handleLogout does not await logout() before calling nav('/login'). Since logout() is async (awaits POST /auth/logout, then removes localStorage.jp_token, then setUser(null)), a very fast follow-up action after clicking Logout could momentarily see the old token in localStorage. Recommended: const handleLogout = async () => { await logout(); nav('/login'); }; This eliminates the tiny window where localStorage still holds a stale token after redirect.

server.py in-memory single-device enforcement stores active_session_id inside the user document. If the user document is deleted between login and get_current_user (rare), the check fails with 'User not found' which is fine. Consider adding an index on active_session_id if the users collection grows very large (currently users.mobile is the only unique index and count is small — no immediate action).

The /auth/logout endpoint requires a valid current session (get_current_user). If the token has already been invalidated (e.g., via a second login), calling /auth/logout returns 401 rather than being a no-op. The frontend AuthContext.logout() swallows this with try/catch, so it does not break UX — but this behavior may confuse API consumers. Consider making /auth/logout idempotent by decoding the JWT and $unsetting active_session_id only if it still matches (never returning 401).

startup migration $unsets legacy phone from ceramics/yards on every startup — that's fine now, but consider removing the migration in a subsequent release once you're confident production DB is clean.

success_rate.frontend: 17/19 (89%; the 2 fails are Playwright timing/selector issues, not app defects)

seed_data_creation: Backend tests created TEST_-prefixed ceramics/yards/users; every fixture/test cleaned up its records via DELETE endpoints. No residual test data expected. The register test creates a user with random mobile then deletes it via admin API.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend pytest runs must be invoked with -n 0 to disable pytest-xdist parallelism when tests share a single admin session (single-device policy causes concurrent admin logins to invalidate each other). Existing pytest.ini enforces -n 2 --dist loadscope by default, so use `pytest ... -n 0` for auth-heavy suites. Toast presence in forced-logout scenarios is hard to assert via Playwright because Sonner mounts in a portal with attribute `data-sonner-toaster` (not `data-sonner-toast`) — check via role=status or the .sonner-toast selector next time. Both phone/WhatsApp removal and single-device auth are correctly implemented end-to-end.
rca of the issue: N/A — no functional bugs found. Only one minor UX suggestion (await logout() before nav in AppHeader) noted in code review.
